records.title: Unsupported data must not become a false zero
records.research_source: Published unsupported-data Result: https://aidemos.com/benchmarks/ai-database-agents/results/futuresmart-ai-database-agent/the-connected-data-cannot-answer-the-question. Separate maintainer reproduction/validation, not an exact historical rerun.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Published Fail, unchanged; separate released engineering fix does not regrade the original run.
records.observed_failure: An unsupported reviews question was answered with zero using unrelated audit records.
records.root_cause: SQL could run on an available table even when that table did not represent the requested metric. Query success was mistaken for answer support.
records.engineering_decision: Require an explicit schema-support decision. Keep genuine zero distinct from unavailable data; preserve table-access and execution-error guards.
records.implementation: Added answerability propagation through SQL generation/execution, final answer and multi-source paths. Clear surrogate SQL/stale rows when unsupported.
records.validation: Focused regressions cover unsupported input, real zero, positive results, denied tables and execution errors. Independent staged browser controls covered missing data, count 0 and count 2; a production missing-data check and a separate real-source positive SQL/rows/chart check passed.
records.limits: A bounded product fix, not a full historical benchmark rerun. Metadata/schema-hint omissions remain separate. The original research verdict is not changed.

records.observed_failure: A valid nested stacked-chart response could be unavailable in the UI despite valid SQL/rows and stored chart data.
records.root_cause: The frontend result contract did not consistently normalize flat and nested segmented chart shapes.
records.engineering_decision: Normalize the supplied result contract; keep individual values, zeros, missing series and Data/Query/Raw views. Do not replace SQL or tune a model to repair a renderer.

records.validation: Component contracts and independent staged/production browser checks passed. A synthetic four-order source produced visible North 100+150 and South 80+120 segments; SQL, all rows and full-reload saved reopen agreed.
records.limits: This fixes rendering. It does not prove that a chart-only follow-up preserves the original business metric, or upgrade the published broad charting result.

records.title: Deliver and save the primary answer before optional work
records.research_source: Maintainer-observed timeout/empty initial UI and measured request-path investigation; no published case-level research result established.
records.historical_benchmark_result: Not publicly verifiable: case-level source is unpublished; no new benchmark verdict
records.observed_failure: The old request waited for the whole graph/chart before its first useful answer. Later transport errors could erase an already received answer or identity.
records.root_cause: Required answer delivery, optional work, persistence acknowledgement and frontend error state shared one fragile completion boundary.
records.engineering_decision: Use one owned request lifecycle; publish an immutable validated primary after existing guards, acknowledge one insert, and scope optional updates by actual row and authorized ownership. Never retry an insert after unknown commit.
records.implementation: A separate candidate implements primary-before-optional delivery, scoped persistence, retained frontend identity/answer, bounded cancellation and saved-answer-status replay. It does not change models or hosted edge timeouts.
records.validation: On one independent real-provider synthetic sales turn, saved answer arrived 10.922 seconds, chart/EOF 14.500 seconds; complete two rows and saved reopen matched the source. Six native lifecycle contracts passed with declared upstream stubs/no provider calls. A native TCP-reset UI check retained the answer and obtained SQL/rows via one automatic saved read.
records.limits: These timings are not a before/after speed comparison, p95 or SaaS accuracy result. With debug disabled, primary wire has no SQL/rows; they reconcile from storage. The reset proxy cannot exclude coalesced later frames, so exclusive-primary-only delivery is not claimed. Final saved-status correction has green CI but independent replay is incomplete. No production promotion.

records.title: Hosted bring-your-own-key uses the owner's key everywhere and fails clearly without it
records.research_source: Maintainer hosted-operation assessment; no benchmark run
records.observed_failure: On the hosted service, table selection, setup description jobs, chart post-processing and embedding clients built provider clients without the owner's key, so they used the platform environment key; a missing or unreadable owner key also fell back to the platform key, and the few-shot store swallowed credential errors into the platform key. A browser session could also name another owner's email on the credential routes.
records.root_cause: Verified in source: key resolution was opt-in per call site and the factory defaulted to environment keys; owner resolution only translated 'me'.
records.engineering_decision: Make the key source an explicit per-owner setting (own | platform, deployment default for unset owners), bind the owner's keys once per request or setup job, and route every environment key read through that binding. Preserve standalone and existing platform-managed owners unchanged. Limit browser sessions to their own credentials. No new authentication system, RBAC framework, prompt or model change.
records.implementation: backend/agent/utils/provider_key_scope.py; nl2sql_owner_config.provider_key_source (migration add_owner_provider_key_source records every existing agent owner as platform); canonicalize_legacy_table_flags converts exact legacy 1/0 table-visibility flags to the booleans the strict access policy reads, leaving malformed or empty maps to fail closed. Coded errors provider_key_missing/invalid/unreadable/rejected/unbound.
records.validation: 87 backend tests in the Linux API image plus 12 deployment checks; the new key tests fail when the old factory environment read is restored. Migrations dry-run on hosted metadata in a rolled-back transaction, then applied after a cluster snapshot. Hosted journey with the existing user, a new agent, a temporary inference-scoped key and a SELECT-only synthetic four-order fixture: setup without a key failed with the missing-key message; with the key, UI description and table setup, one question returned the exact SQL, two rows (South 200, North 250) and a bar chart; the saved conversation reopened intact; logs showed only owner-key use and OpenAI usage attributed requests only to the temporary key; after removing the key in the UI the next question failed with the clear message before any model call or SQL. A platform-sourced owner still answered via the platform key. Temporary key, service account, agent, fixture and network rule were removed.

Agents without any table-visibility record fail closed until their owner reviews visibility. Not a benchmark run; historical verdicts unchanged.

records.title: Saved conversations stay on their agent and under its answer settings
records.research_source: Maintainer security review after the MCP adapter (public PR 6); no benchmark run
records.observed_failure: Chat history and saved replay were read by session_id alone, so a caller allowed to use agent A could pass a session id from agent B and have B's questions and answers replayed into A's model context and appended to B's session. Saved replay returned SQL and rows for agents set to hide them (show_sql_query / show_db_result applied only to live answers), CSV export ignored show_db_result, an agent key could export another agent's turn through a caller-chosen agent_id, and feedback could rewrite another agent's stored verdict and SQL.
records.root_cause: Verified in source: the ChatLogs reads behind history, replay, export lookup and feedback filtered by session_id (and chat_id) only; the visibility flags were applied in build_chat_response alone.
records.engineering_decision: Put the isolation in the reads, not in a session-ownership gate: every read of a conversation's turns filters on the requesting agent, and a session this API created for another agent is refused (404) before allowance, history or model. A session id the API never created (the platform chat service sends its own thread id; 4,972 such sessions measured on hosted) continues with this agent's turns only - a strict 404 for unknown ids, as first ported from public PR 6, was rejected in independent review because it would have broken that service. Replay applies the same visibility flags as live chat at the API; get_session_data requires agent_id and both flags. No new authentication framework, model, prompt or SQL change.

records.title: The public API lives at futuresmart.ai/database-agent/api
records.research_source: Product URL strategy (one FutureSmart identity, no product subdomains); no benchmark run
records.observed_failure: The public API root was the application host (app.futuresmart.ai/nl2sql/api; the Share page printed agent.futuresmart.ai/nl2sql/api). The default API docs page built absolute /nl2sql/api URLs from the mount, so it could not work under any other root. The hosted app pages declared robots index, follow.
records.root_cause: Verified in source and on live: FastAPI's default docs_url page and openapi servers derive from the mount's root_path; the repository's own relative /docs route was shadowed by it.
records.engineering_decision: Expose the canonical root as an nginx location on the futuresmart.ai web server (written by the website's deploy script, raw request URI forwarded, buffering off) that forwards through app.futuresmart.ai to the same ECS service: no second backend, no new auth, /nl2sql/api unchanged. The docs app turns the default page off, loads openapi.json by a relative URL and names PUBLIC_API_ROOT as its server when set. App pages noindex at the edge (CloudFront X-Robots-Tag) and in the page meta.
records.implementation: backend/swaggers/public_root.py, backend/swaggers/nl2sql.py; task definition env PUBLIC_API_ROOT. Elsewhere: FutureSmart-AI/futuresmart-website PRs 106 (routing) and 107 (landing samples, MCP); database-agent-ui PR 9; document-intelligence-ui PR 6; database-agent PR 8 (docs); CloudFront response-headers policy fs-app-noindex on E2LZUHAF1FR08.
records.validation: tests/backend/test_public_api_root.py (4). Hosted, task definition 209 (main-dbcd415), temporary synthetic agents through https://futuresmart.ai/database-agent/api: the production journey's isolation, replay-setting, key-scope and MCP stdio checks all pass; streamed answer's first chunk 1.8 s before the end (legacy root 2.0 s); CSV export 200 through both roots for a 120-row turn (a 10-row turn has no file by the 50-row rule on both roots); a conversation made through the new root replays through /nl2sql/api; encoded paths (%2F, %20, +, //) forwarded byte for byte. Signed-in hosted UI: Share page prints the new root; a saved conversation replays with SQL and rows.
records.limits: Requests through the new root reach CloudFront from the website server's address, so the app distribution's per-IP WAF rate rule (Count mode today) would see them as one client if it were switched to Block. Document Intelligence chat through its new root was not exercised end to end (authenticated reads were).

records.title: Model evaluation through the real API, and per-answer latency and cost
records.research_source: Model evaluation and optimisation initiative (accuracy, latency, cost of model configurations)
records.observed_failure: No repeatable way to compare model configurations on ground truth; hosted answers carried no cost (DA-COST-001) and table selection's model call was never counted.
records.root_cause: Cost depended on LangSmith pricing, which is off on hosted; per-node metrics covered only the nodes that recorded themselves.
records.engineering_decision: Evaluate through the existing chat API and Compose stack (no separate SQL agent or service); grade with an LLM judge against twice-computed ground truth; estimate cost from recorded tokens and a dated price table, with totals from a run-level callback so uninstrumented calls cannot disappear.

records.title: One development repository: hosted interface and public repository produced from it
records.research_source: Maintainer decision (repository consolidation), not a benchmark finding
records.observed_failure: The hosted interface was built from a separate UI repository and the public repository carried its own edits (MCP server), so changes merged in the development repository (the usage panel) were not live and public-only work was absent from development.
records.root_cause: The 2026-10-20 consolidation imported the UI but left its repository deploying production, and the public repository was edited directly after its first export.
records.engineering_decision: Bring every change that existed only in the UI or public repository into the development repository; deploy the hosted interface from it; produce the public repository only by an exporter that refuses to overwrite direct public edits; archive the UI repository.
